headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Roo Code can write/egress broadly while Prefect can orchestrate networked workflows, creating dangerous default paths for leakage, conflicts, and cascading automation errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads and writes VS Code workspace files and uses MCP; Prefect can call APIs and has broad network egress. If Prefect-generated artifacts land in the shared workspace, Roo Code may treat them as trusted instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes injection plausible, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Prefect writes untrusted text into the shared workspace
IF Roo Code parses workspace files as instructions or tool directives
IF an MCP server relays Prefect output into Roo Code without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Disable MCP connections that ingest untrusted text
Mark Prefect outputs as data-only in filenames and headers
Add a manual review step before Roo Code acts on generated files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys; Prefect has broad network egress and API-calling capability. In a shared workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can be exposed if Prefect reads or uploads files. The leakage path is plausible in default workspace-sharing setups, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share the same workspace directory
IF Prefect reads files that Roo Code writes
IF Prefect sends workspace contents to external APIs
mitigations: Use separate repositories or workspace roots
Restrict Prefect to non-sensitive folders
Disable file-upload steps in Prefect flows
Rotate or scope model-provider API keys
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; Prefect can also operate over files and networked workflows. Both agents can mutate the same workspace, and Roo Code explicitly shares state via filesystem across instances. Without locking, concurrent edits and git changes can corrupt work or overwrite each other.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same VS Code workspace
IF Prefect writes files that Roo Code also edits
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without locks
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits git state
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Enable explicit file-locking around shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on files and browser state, while Prefect can generate workflow artifacts and trigger API calls. If Prefect outputs are treated as authoritative by Roo Code, errors can cascade into automated edits or external actions. The pair lacks documented verification boundaries, so the safer higher severity is high.
conditions: IF Prefect-produced text is fed into Roo Code as task instructions
IF Roo Code executes edits or browser actions based on that text
IF no human verification step exists between generation and action
mitigations: Require human approval before Roo Code acts on Prefect output
Add a verification checklist for generated artifacts
Limit Prefect to producing drafts only
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and touch workflow metadata or source code, with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or GDPR mismatch shown. The main compliance concern is generic retention/logging rather than a documented jurisdictional breach. Because no stronger mismatch is evidenced, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent logs or retains that data beyond policy
IF deployment jurisdiction imposes residency rules not reflected in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workspaces
Review logging settings for both agents
Set short retention on generated artifacts
Document data-class handling rules
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
